scope: docs/41-试点课堂Start持久迁移内核SDD.md §109

findings.title: Lock acquisition failure can poison shared health during another active writer
findings.detail: Lock acquisition failures poison shared health without owning the global catalog lock. Another local operation may already hold that lock and have passed its under-lock health recheck, then continue writing after the health flag is poisoned.
findings.recommendation: Serialize full local catalog critical sections and poison transitions with a supervisor-wide operation gate, or explicitly narrow the contract; add a deterministic test with one writer paused after its health recheck and another caller's injected lock failure.

findings.title: Limit exhaustion must poison supervisor globally
findings.evidence: Transition poisons shared health on frame and byte limits; test verifies future Snapshot rejection.

findings.title: Require shared health and recheck under lock
findings.evidence: Constructors reject nil health; all mutating/read entry points perform a post-lock health check.

findings.title: Poison before unlock after startup/read failures
findings.evidence: Deterministic unlock-window barrier tests startup Sync and Snapshot read errors.

findings.title: Cross-process file lock test and platform implementations
findings.evidence: Self-spawned process contention test plus Unix flock and Windows LockFileEx implementations; OS-specific tagged execution remains an integration gate.

findings.title: Reject noncanonical JSON frames
findings.evidence: Decoder byte-compares canonical re-encoding; tests cover reordered fields, whitespace, unknown/duplicate keys, and trailing object.

integration_gates: Run pilot_e2e tagged tests on Windows and POSIX CI.
Wire one supervisor-owned pilotCatalogHealth into every issued journal and enforce OpenVerified/bootstrap/ACL contracts from §109.
